topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecturer, sets out the scope of the lecture series, and outlines the key learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Foundations of cancer causation: genetics, bad luck, and environmental exposure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the conceptual framework of cancer etiology by examining how intrinsic stochastic mutations, inherited genetics, and external environmental exposures interact to drive malignancy across populations.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological agents drive oncogenesis, illustrated in detail by the viral and environmental etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Direct and metabolic mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and chemical compounds interact with cellular metabolism to induce DNA adducts, oxidative stress, and mutations.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, microenvironment, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic drivers of cancer development, including the two-stage model of promotion, inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental stages of host vulnerability.

topics.label: Methodologies for detecting and assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, experimental, and risk-assessment frameworks used to determine whether exposures cause cancer.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the final closing remarks and summarizes the overarching takeaways of the lecture.
